name: Hobbywing V5 OPTO layout
rationale:
The layout was chosen by a PROFILE KEY. profileKey() returned
`<hardware_version>_PL_OPTO` for any OPTO model, and PROFILES carried exactly one such
entry, HW1104_V100456NB_PL_OPTO -- so every OTHER OPTO model missed the lookup, fell
through to PROFILES.default, and got DEFAULT_ITEMS: bec_voltage at item 5,
active_freewheel at 15, where OPTO_ITEMS has no bec_voltage and puts
active_freewheel at 14. An OPTO ESC has no BEC byte, so every field from item 5 up
was read and written one byte off, on a page that looked entirely normal. Measured
on the codec's own simulator fixture, 9 of the 15 fields on the OPTO layout read
the wrong byte, plus a phantom bec_voltage row over a byte the block does not have.
Six of the 15 coincide: four sit before the missing byte, and two carry equal bytes
on either side of the boundary in this fixture.

OPTO was also looked for in ONE of the two model strings. The block carries the
model twice -- bytes 35..50 as esc_type and 51..65 as mode_name -- plus the
firmware version in bytes 3..18, and which of the three a given ESC puts "OPTO" in
is not something this file can know. EdgeTX concatenates both model strings for
exactly that reason (esc_parameters_hw5.lua:119, :251).

The VARIANT chooses the LAYOUT and the VERSION chooses the CHOICE LISTS:
profileFor() looks the version up as before and then, for an OPTO model, returns
that profile's tables with OPTO_ITEMS. An explicit `<version>_PL_OPTO` entry still
wins where one exists, because its tables may differ -- HW1104's do not, but that is
a fact about HW1104. The merged profile is built once per version rather than per
call, because isFieldAvailable() reaches profileFor() once per field per page build.

ON THE ISSUE'S SECOND CLAIM -- the inverted Active Freewheel boolean -- this job
changes nothing, and that is the finding. Both suites say 0 = Enabled, 1 = Disabled
(here msp_esc_parameters_hw5.lua:21, and EdgeTX's esc_forward_hw5 page:687-690),
the codec passes the byte through untouched in both directions, and the flight
controller treats the whole HW5 block as opaque and only ever memcmps it
(esc_sensor.c:2387-2393). The issue itself writes "0 = Enabled vs 1 = Disabled, or
vice versa depending on firmware version" -- a question, not a specification. So
there is nothing here to invert. The parity check is a plain check rather than a
gate, and it exists so the answer stays a fact the repository carries.

Deliberately NOT in this pull request: FIELD_META declares startup_time as min 4,
max 25, default 11 while decode() hands the page the raw byte, which runs 0..21, so
the row violates its own range. That is a real defect, but it lives in decode() and
encode() rather than in the layout, it affects every HW5 model whether OPTO or not,
and EdgeTX settles it by adding 4 on the way in and taking 4 off on the way out
(esc_parameters_hw5.lua:263-265, :296-298). It has its own harness and its own job.

12 of its 31 checks go red without the fix. Pass --self-test to prove that: it
splices the pre-fix profile selection back into a copy of the codec and requires
every one of the twelve to fail -- and verifies the splice four ways first, because
a sabotage that breaks the module differently from the defect under test proves
nothing. One case started out as a gate and the self-test caught it passing on the
pre-fix code, which is why it is a plain check now: OPTO hardware HW1104, because
that model already worked -- PROFILES carried an entry for it.
